title: Narrative Paradoxes in LLM Inference: Shaping Reasoning Trajectories toward Misalignment
abstract: arXiv:2610.16312v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Explicit reasoning in large language models (LLMs) is often associated with reliability, yet it can still pose risks when a model infers harmful goals under a benign context. We identify a distinct challenge: ensuring the safety of the \emph{multi-step reasoning process} itself, where locally coherent steps may still lead to globally harmful outcomes. To explore this vulnerability, we propose PDRA (Paradox-driven Reasoning-based Attack), a novel attack method that programs a harmful reasoning trajectory. PDRA first constructs a paradoxical narrative core by pairing a malicious actor (e.g., a terrorist) with a benign task (e.g., writing a safety bulletin). It then embeds this core into a structured analytical framework that forces the model through a mandatory three-stage analysis -- surface purpose, latent intent, and operational reconstruction -- guiding it to produce detailed harmful content while maintaining narrative coherence. translated_title: 大语言模型推理中的叙事悖论：将推理轨迹引向对齐失调
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）中的显式推理通常被认为与可靠性相关联，然而当模型在良性语境下推断出有害目标时，它仍可能构成风险。我们识别出一个独特的挑战：确保多步推理过程本身的安全性，即局部连贯的推理步骤仍可能导致全局有害的结果。为探索这一漏洞，我们提出了PDRA（悖论驱动的推理攻击），这是一种新颖的攻击方法，能够对有害的推理轨迹进行编程。PDRA首先通过将恶意行为者（如恐怖分子）与良性任务（如撰写安全公告）配对，构建一个悖论式叙事核心。然后将该核心嵌入一个结构化分析框架中，迫使模型经历强制性的三阶段分析——表面目的、潜在意图和操作重建——引导模型在保持叙事连贯性的同时产生详细的有害内容。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种名为PDRA的新型攻击方法，通过将恶意行为者与良性任务配对构建悖论叙事核心，并利用强制性的三阶段分析框架引导模型的多步推理轨迹，揭示了大语言模型显式推理过程本身的安全漏洞。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes PDRA, a novel attack method that constructs a paradoxical narrative core by pairing a malicious actor with a benign task and forces the model through a mandatory three-stage analysis, steering LLM multi-step reasoning trajectories toward producing harmful content while maintaining narrative coherence.
